clue.text: A shear delight to their owners ?

definitions.text: A shear delight to their owners ?

parts.words: A shear delight to their owners
parts.note: 'shear' sounds like 'sheer': young female sheep, kept for wool, are a delight to the farmer who shears them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue turns on 'shear' for 'sheer': a sheer delight, and one that can be shorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Young female sheep grow fleeces that their keepers clip each year, so they bring pleasure at shearing time.

clue.text: Side number

definitions.meaning: a team, as in cricket or football, which fields this many players

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team fields eleven players and is called by that figure; it is also simply a number.

clue.text: Prize for a champion hen?

parts.note: a trophy cup for a prize-winning bird would naturally be a cup for eggs

explanation.walkthrough: Champions win cups; a hen's cup would hold an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup for holding a boiled egg at breakfast.

clue.text: Hat trimmed with cards for a true friend

indicators.note: a hat trimmed with something has it all round the edge, so those letters surround the hat

parts.note: aces are playing cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hat decorated with playing cards as a gift for a loyal friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmed with' looks like cut short, but it means edged, as a hat is trimmed with ribbon. Achates is the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid, Achates is Aeneas's loyal companion, a byword for a faithful comrade.

clue.text: Journey's end for John Gilpin

parts.note: in Cowper's comic ballad, John Gilpin's runaway horse carries him to an inn at Edmonton named after something that rings

explanation.walkthrough: Cowper's ballad 'John Gilpin' has the hero's wife waiting at the Bell inn at Edmonton, where his ride should end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bell at Edmonton is the inn that was the planned destination in Cowper's ballad.

clue.text: Speaker more tedious than inflammatory, though

definitions.text: Speaker more tedious than inflammatory, though

parts.words: Speaker more tedious than inflammatory, though
parts.note: a long-winded talker is called a balloon full of gas, and gas can be inflammable, though this talker merely bores

explanation.walkthrough: A balloon's envelope of gas could catch fire, but the windbag talker is only dull, not inflammatory in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a windbag who talks at tiresome length, from the image of a bag full of hot air.

clue.text: By derivation the driest state in America?

definitions.text: By derivation the driest state in America?

parts.words: By derivation the driest state in America
parts.note: the state's name is said to come from words meaning arid zone, so by its origin it is the driest

explanation.walkthrough: The name is popularly derived from 'arida zona', a dry belt; the true origin is disputed, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A south-western US state whose name is popularly traced to a phrase meaning dry region.

clue.text: But it surely couldn't measure a rood.!

definitions.text: But it surely couldn't measure a rood.!

parts.words: But it surely couldn't measure a rood
parts.note: a rood is a quarter-acre of land; the word for an entrance read from its back gives rood, though no doorway could measure that much

explanation.walkthrough: Spell DOOR from the back and you get ROOD, a land measure of a quarter acre; but a rear entrance is never that size.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear entrance to a house, at the back of the building.

clue.text: They achieve stardom in the American wars

definitions.text: They achieve stardom in the American wars

parts.words: They achieve stardom in the American wars
parts.note: senior US army officers wear stars as rank insignia, so they win stars in war

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stardom' looks like fame, but American senior officers' rank is shown by stars on the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Top military commanders, who in the US army wear one to five stars.

clue.text: Its breaking caused civil commotion in Lilliput

definitions.text: Its breaking caused civil commotion in Lilliput

parts.words: Its breaking caused civil commotion in Lilliput
parts.note: in Gulliver's Travels, Lilliput fought a civil war over which end of a boiled egg to crack open

explanation.walkthrough: Swift's Big-Endians and Little-Endians quarrelled over the right end at which to break a breakfast egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin outer casing of an egg is what the Lilliputians argued about cracking.

clue.text: Its contents may improve one's bearing

definitions.text: Its contents may improve one's bearing

parts.words: Its contents may improve one's bearing
parts.note: 'bearing' is a machine part that runs smoother with lubrication, not a person's posture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like deportment, but it is the ball or roller bearing in a machine, which lubricant helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A small vessel with a spout for squirting lubricant into machinery.

clue.text: Payments for letters ?

parts.note: 'letters' means people who let property, not written messages

explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like post, but it means those who let houses; what they receive is rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums paid regularly by tenants to landlords for hired property.

clue.text: Fair play for players

definitions.meaning: the British actors' trade union is named ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses; 'players' means actors here.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed justice is one sense; the other is the name of the performers' trade union.

clue.text: A promotion type

parts.note: read as 'a pro-motion type': someone in favour of a motion at a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests advancement at work; split it as 'pro-motion', the person who backs a proposal after it is made.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal meeting, the person who supports a proposal so it can be debated.

clue.text: Such is the state of a pixie in a Herts town

indicators.note: the small creature is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire
an elf is a pixie-like sprite

explanation.surface: Asking about the condition of a sprite living in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, a county north of London; 'Such is the state' points to the phrase for Britain's system of social security.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's postwar system of public social provision is called the welfare state.

clue.text: In 10, a must, it seems ?

parts.note: the lubricant found inside an oilcan (10 across) looks, from the clue, like one that is indispensable

explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is OILCAN; what is in it is oil, and 'a must' suggests the oil is necessary. Really it is a perfume extract from plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated aromatic extract distilled from plants, used in scents.

clue.text: They're one over the eight and associated with beer

definitions.text: They're one over the eight and associated with beer

parts.words: They're one over the eight and associated with beer
parts.note: a set of pins numbers nine, one more than eight, and the old saying pairs beer with a pub game

explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being drunk, but here it is literally nine pins; 'life is not all beer and skittles' is an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub game of knocking down nine wooden pins with a ball.

clue.text: Grey-coat mixed class

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A school class in grey uniforms, boys and girls together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges GREYCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group or division of things of the same kind.

clue.text: Not another name for blackjack

parts.note: the black-suited jack in a pack of cards; 'blackjack' also names a cosh and a card game, but here it is a jack in a black suit

explanation.walkthrough: A jack is also called a knave, and clubs is a black suit, so a 'black jack' can fairly be named this way; 'Not' warns it is not the card game or the cosh.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack of the clubs suit is a black jack, a knave being the old word for jack.

clue.text: He spelt her name differently

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are set out in another order

explanation.surface: A man wrote a woman's name with an unusual spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges HE SPELT into a Scottish woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish form of Elizabeth, a woman's given name.

clue.text: Music-maker made the Wedding Guest beat his breast

definitions.text: Music-maker made the Wedding Guest beat his breast

parts.words: Music-maker made the Wedding Guest beat his breast
parts.note: in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner the Wedding-Guest beats his breast on hearing a loud woodwind instrument

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge: 'The Wedding-Guest here beat his breast, For he heard the loud bassoon.'
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-toned woodwind instrument, the one heard at the feast in Coleridge's poem.

clue.text: Just the vehicle for the backseat driver

definitions.text: Just the vehicle for the backseat driver

parts.words: Just the vehicle for the backseat driver
parts.note: a backseat driver usually nags from behind; in this horse-drawn cab the driver really sits high at the back

explanation.walkthrough: In a two-wheeled cab of this kind the driver's seat is mounted behind the passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn cab with the driver perched behind.

clue.text: Eccentricity seems to make a child a favourite'

definitions.text: Eccentricity seems to make a child a favourite'

parts.words: Eccentricity seems to make a child a favourite
parts.note: an odd boy, a boy who is odd, read as one word for a betting favourite

explanation.walkthrough: Split as ODD'S SON, the eccentric's offspring; together it is the betting term for a likely winner.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a runner priced shorter than evens, the expected winner.

clue.text: Novel piece' of land with rich potentialities

definitions.meaning: a famous adventure book by Robert Louis Stevenson

definitions.text: piece' of land with rich potentialities
definitions.meaning: a stretch of land surrounded by sea that may hold buried riches

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'piece of land'; the apostrophe is an OCR stray.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's pirate story is one sense; literally, an isle where hoarded gold might be dug up.

clue.text: See 23
Midsummer night flier

parts.note: an insect flying on a summer night; also one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Dream has a fairy named Moth among Titania's attendants, and the insect flies at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-flying insect, and the name of a fairy in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: He makes one ill

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are made into a name, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man whose presence brings on sickness in someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges ONE ILL into a man's name; 'He' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so it can stand for a 'he'.

clue.text: Mr. Big takes care of us without loss

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the other letters wrap around the word for loss

parts.note: c/o is the abbreviation for care of on an envelope
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big shot looks after the rest of us without any loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'care of' is the c/o written on envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant statue or anything enormous; a figure of great size, like a 'Mr Big'.

clue.text: Chesty complication of Father Time

indicators.note: a complication tangles things up, so the letters of the word that follows are mixed

explanation.surface: Father Time with a chest complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complication of' rearranges CHESTY; the definition is Father Time's emblem, the blade he carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Time is pictured carrying a long curved blade for mowing, his attribute.

clue.text: " Birds in their little nests agree, With-—-but not with me" (Belloc)

definitions.text: Birds in their little nests agree, With-—-but not with me

parts.words: Birds in their little nests agree, With-—-but not with me
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hilaire Belloc's verse; the missing word is the people from a large Asian country

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a quotation with a word blanked out; Belloc's couplet ends 'With Chinamen, but not with me', an old-fashioned term now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Belloc's couplet, an old term for people from a large East Asian country.
